summary: Every read is a server-rendered response from one Rust binary behind CloudFront. Nothing is always on, and the only persistent state is a disposable table of check runs.

nodes.label: Browser
nodes.role: Reads HTML. No JavaScript is required for any content on this site.

nodes.label: Route 53
nodes.role: Alias records at the apex, which is why DNS lives here rather than at the registrar.

nodes.label: CloudFront
nodes.role: Behaviour precedence is load-bearing: the POST endpoints are ordered ahead of the read-only default, which allows only GET and HEAD.

nodes.label: Cache policy
nodes.role: Short TTL with ETag revalidation for HTML. Per-visitor responses are no-store, not briefly cached.

nodes.label: Function URL
nodes.role: No API Gateway. Nothing here needs a custom authorizer, usage plan, or request validation.

nodes.label: site-handler
nodes.role: One Rust binary routing every page and API path with axum. arm64 on provided.al2023.

nodes.label: Fit workflow
nodes.role: Express, invoked synchronously. Extract, then four parallel matchers that each apply a different rule, then aggregate.

nodes.label: Provenance workflow
nodes.role: Standard and asynchronous, because a dozen outbound checks with timeouts will not finish inside a request.

nodes.label: Task functions
nodes.role: One binary per workflow, dispatching on a tagged payload. The matchers are pure compute with identical permissions, so separate artifacts would be copies.

nodes.label: Runs table
nodes.role: Check-run projections, on-demand, with a TTL on every item. Reads render from the projection and make zero Step Functions calls.

nodes.label: Log groups
nodes.role: Retention set explicitly on every one. The default never expires and becomes the largest line item on a project this size.

nodes.label: Alarms
nodes.role: Failed executions on both workflows, plus handler errors and throttles. The fit workflow falls back to inline analysis, so without an alarm a broken workflow is invisible.

nodes.label: Alert topic
nodes.role: One topic for the stack. The subscriber address comes from deploy context, never from a file in the repository.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions
nodes.role: Assumes a deploy role by OIDC. No long-lived access keys exist in the repository or in CI secrets.

nodes.label: ACM certificate
nodes.role: A separate stack in us-east-1, because CloudFront accepts certificates from no other region.
